quote: (ii) The head of the contracting activity has determined, based upon a preponderance of the evidence, that the Contractor or someone acting for the Contractor has engaged in conduct punishable under 41 U.S.C. 2105(a).

statement: If the Government rescinds the contract under paragraph (a), the Government is entitled to recover, in addition to any penalty prescribed by law, the amount expended under the contract.
quote: (b) If the Government rescinds the contract under paragraph (a) of this clause, the Government is entitled to recover, in addition to any penalty prescribed by law, the amount expended under the contract.

statement: The Price or Fee Adjustment for Illegal or Improper Activity clause is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.104-9(b).
quote: As prescribed in 3.104-9(b) insert the following clause:

statement: The Government, at its election, may reduce the price of a fixed-price type contract and the total cost and fee under a cost-type contract by the amount of profit or fee determined under paragraph (b) of the clause, conditional on a determination by the head of the contracting activity or designee.
quote: (a) The Government, at its election, may reduce the price of a fixed-price type contract and the total cost and fee under a cost-type contract by the amount of profit or fee determined as set forth in paragraph (b) of this clause if the head of the contracting activity or designee determines

statement: The determination that supports the price or fee reduction is a determination by the head of the contracting activity or designee that there was a violation of 41 U.S.C. 2102 or 2103, as implemented in section 3.104 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation.
quote: if the head of the contracting activity or designee determines that there was a violation of 41 U.S.C. 2102 or 2103, as implemented in section 3.104 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation.

statement: For cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the price or fee reduction is the amount of the fee specified in the contract at the time of award.
quote: (b) The price or fee reduction referred to in paragraph (a) of this clause shall be— (1) For cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the amount of the fee specified in the contract at the time of award;

statement: For firm-fixed-price contracts, the price or fee reduction is 10 percent of the initial contract price or a profit amount determined by the Contracting Officer from records or documents in existence prior to the date of the contract award.
quote: (5) For firm-fixed-price contracts, by 10 percent of the initial contract price or a profit amount determined by the Contracting Officer from records or documents in existence prior to the date of the contract award.

statement: The Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct clause is to be inserted as prescribed in FAR 3.1004(a).
quote: As prescribed in 3.1004(a), insert the following clause:

statement: The clause requires the Contractor to timely disclose, in writing, to the agency Office of the Inspector General, with a copy to the Contracting Officer, whenever, in connection with the award, performance, or closeout of this contract or any subcontract under it, the Contractor has credible evidence of the conduct that the clause goes on to list.

statement: If an offeror provides a disclosure under paragraph (e) of 52.204-29, the contracting officer shall engage with the program office or requiring activity to determine whether to pursue a waiver, if available.
quote: If an offeror provides a disclosure pursuant to paragraph (e) of 52.204-29, Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act Orders—Representation and Disclosures, the contracting officer shall engage with the program office or requiring activity to determine whether to pursue a waiver, if available

statement: A request for waiver shall be submitted by the executive agency in writing to the official that issued the order, unless other instructions for submission are provided by the applicable FASCSA order.
quote: A request for waiver shall be submitted by the executive agency in writing to the official that issued the order, unless other instructions for submission are provided by the applicable FASCSA order.

statement: If a waiver is being pursued, the contracting officer may not make an award until written approval is obtained that the waiver has been granted.
quote: If a waiver is being pursued, then the contracting officer may not make an award until written approval is obtained that the waiver has been granted.

statement: In all Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts where FASCSA orders are applied at the order level, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-28.
quote: (a) In all Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts where FASCSA orders are applied at the order level, the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-28,

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.204-29, Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act Orders—Representation and Disclosures, in all solicitations, except for Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts.
quote: (b) The contracting officer shall insert the provision at 52.204-29, Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act Orders—Representation and Disclosures— (1) In all solicitations, except for Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts.

statement: The clause at 52.204-30 shall be inserted in solicitations and contracts if the conditions specified at 4.2304(a)(1) apply, except for Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts.
quote: shall insert the clause at 52.204-30, Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act Orders—Prohibition— (1) In solicitations and contracts if the conditions specified at 4.2304(a)(1) apply, except for Federal Supply Schedules, Governmentwide acquisition contracts, and multi-agency contracts.

statement: Offerors and quoters are required to complete electronic annual representations and certifications in SAM as a part of required registration, with a cross-reference to FAR 4.1102.
quote: Offerors and quoters are required to complete electronic annual representations and certifications in SAM accessed via https://www.sam.gov as a part of required registration (see FAR 4.1102).

statement: Representations and certifications submitted to SAM are to be reviewed and updated as necessary, but at least annually, to keep them current, accurate, and complete, and they are effective until one year from date of submission or update to SAM.
quote: required to review and update the representations and certifications submitted to SAM as necessary, but at least annually, to ensure they are kept current, accurate, and complete. The representations and certifications are effective until one year from date of submission or update to SAM.

statement: The provision at 52.204-8, Annual Representations and Certifications, is to be inserted in solicitations, except for solicitations for commercial products or commercial services issued under part 12.
quote: Insert the provision at 52.204-8, Annual Representations and Certifications, in solicitations, except for solicitations for commercial products or commercial services issued under part 12.

statement: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-19, Incorporation by Reference of Representations and Certifications, in solicitations and contracts.
quote: The contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.204-19, Incorporation by Reference of Representations and Certifications, in solicitations and contracts.

statement: The PIID shall be used to identify all solicitation and contract actions.
quote: The PIID shall be used to identify all solicitation and contract actions.

statement: The PIID consists of a combination of thirteen to seventeen alpha and/or numeric characters, and special characters such as hyphens, dashes, or spaces are not used.
quote: (a) Elements of a PIID. The PIID consists of a combination of thirteen to seventeen alpha and/or numeric characters sequenced to convey certain information. Do not use special characters (such as hyphens, dashes, or spaces).

statement: One listed element of the PIID is that the first six positions identify the department/agency and office issuing the instrument, using the AAC assigned to the issuing office.
quote: (1) Positions 1 through 6. The first six positions identify the department/agency and office issuing the instrument. Use the AAC assigned to the issuing office for positions 1 through 6.

statement: One listed element of the PIID is that the seventh and eighth positions are the last two digits of the fiscal year in which the instrument is issued or awarded, measured by the date the action is signed rather than the effective date if different.
quote: (2) Positions 7 through 8. The seventh and eighth positions are the last two digits of the fiscal year in which the procurement instrument is issued or awarded. This is the date the action is signed, not the effective date if the effective date is different.

statement: One listed element of the PIID is that position nine indicates the type of instrument by one of the listed upper case letters.
quote: (3) Position 9. Indicate the type of instrument by entering one of the following upper case letters in position nine.

statement: Amendments to solicitations are numbered sequentially using a four position numeric serial number, beginning with 0001, in addition to the 13-17 character PIID.
quote: (1) Amendments to solicitations. Number amendments to solicitations sequentially using a four position numeric serial number in addition to the 13-17 character PIID beginning with 0001.

statement: Modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements are numbered using a six position alpha or numeric, or a combination thereof, in addition to the 13-17 character PIID.
quote: (2) Modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements. Number modifications to contracts, orders, and agreements using a six position alpha or numeric, or a combination thereof, in addition to the 13-17 character PIID.

statement: Contracting officers shall distribute copies of contracts or modifications within 10 working days after execution by all parties.
quote: Contracting officers shall distribute copies of contracts or modifications within 10 working days after execution by all parties.

statement: The Federal Government shall use electronic commerce whenever practicable or cost-effective.
quote: The Federal Government shall use electronic commerce whenever practicable or cost-effective.

statement: The second listed reporting category covers all fixed-price service contracts awarded and orders issued according to listed thresholds.
quote: (ii) All fixed-price service contracts awarded and orders issued according to the following thresholds:

statement: One listed reporting threshold covers all cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, and labor-hour service contracts and orders with an estimated total value above the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: (2) Reporting is required according to the following thresholds: (i) All cost-reimbursement, time-and-materials, and labor-hour service contracts and orders with an estimated total value above the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: One listed threshold under the fixed-price category is an estimated total value of $500,000 or greater for contracts awarded or orders issued in Fiscal Year 2016 and subsequent years.
quote: (C) Awarded or issued in Fiscal Year 2016, and subsequent years, with an estimated total value of $500,000 or greater.

statement: If the agency believes revisions to contractor reported information are warranted, it shall notify the contractor no later than November 15, and by November 30 the contractor shall revise the report or document its rationale for the agency.
quote: In the event the agency believes that revisions to the contractor reported information are warranted, the agency shall notify the contractor no later than November 15. By November 30, the contractor shall revise the report, or document its rationale for the agency.

statement: Information not collected in FPDS will be provided by the contractor, as specified in the two service contract reporting clauses.
quote: Information not collected in FPDS will be provided by the contractor, as specified in 52.204-14, Service Contract Reporting Requirements and 52.204-15, Service Contract Reporting Requirements for Indefinite-Delivery Contracts.

statement: The apprentice definition includes a person employed and individually registered in a bona fide apprenticeship program registered with the Department of Labor's Office of Apprenticeship Training, Employer, and Labor Services (OATELS) or with a State Apprenticeship Agency recognized by OATELS.
quote: (1) Employed and individually registered in a bona fide apprenticeship program registered with the U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Apprenticeship Training, Employer, and Labor Services (OATELS), or with a State Apprenticeship Agency recognized by OATELS;

statement: One listed alternative in the apprentice definition covers a person in the first 90 days of probationary employment as an apprentice in an apprenticeship program who is not individually registered in the program but has been certified by OATELS or a State Apprenticeship Agency (where appropriate) to be eligible.
quote: (2) Who is in the first 90 days of probationary employment as an apprentice in an apprenticeship program, and is not individually registered in the program, but who has been certified by the OATELS or a State Apprenticeship Agency (where appropriate) to be eligible

statement: Construction, alteration, or repair means all types of work done by laborers and mechanics employed by the construction contractor or subcontractor on a particular building or work at the site thereof, including without limitation the listed types of work.
quote: Construction, alteration, or repair means all types of work done by laborers and mechanics employed by the construction contractor or construction subcontractor on a particular building or work at the site thereof, including without limitations—

statement: The definition of laborers or mechanics includes workers, used by a contractor or subcontractor at any tier, whose duties are manual or physical in nature, as distinguished from mental or managerial.
quote: Laborers or mechanics — (1) Means— (i) Workers, utilized by a contractor or subcontractor at any tier, whose duties are manual or physical in nature (including those workers who use tools or who are performing the work of a trade), as distinguished from mental or managerial;

statement: A public building or public work is building or work whose construction, prosecution, completion, or repair is carried on directly by authority of, or with funds of, a Federal agency to serve the interest of the general public.
quote: Public building or public work means building or work, the construction, prosecution, completion, or repair of which, as defined in this section, is carried on directly by authority of, or with funds of, a Federal agency to serve the interest of the general public

statement: The definition of site of the work includes the primary site, which is the physical place or places where the construction called for in the contract will remain when work on it is completed.
quote: Site of the work — (1) Means— (i) The primary site of the work. The physical place or places where the construction called for in the contract will remain when work on it is completed; and

statement: A trainee is a person registered and receiving on-the-job training in a construction occupation under a program approved in advance by the U.S. Department of Labor, and the definition goes on to name the approving office and add conditions.
quote: Trainee means a person registered and receiving on-the-job training in a construction occupation under a program which has been approved in advance by the U.S. Department of Labor

statement: The definition of wages includes the basic hourly rate of pay and any contribution irrevocably made by a contractor or subcontractor to a trustee or third person under a bona fide fringe benefit fund, plan, or program.
quote: Wages means the basic hourly rate of pay; any contribution irrevocably made by a contractor or subcontractor to a trustee or to a third person pursuant to a bona fide fringe benefit fund, plan, or program;

statement: The requirements of the subpart apply only if the construction work is, or reasonably can be foreseen to be, performed at a particular site so that wage rates can be determined for the locality, and only to construction work performed by laborers and mechanics at the site of the work.
quote: The requirements of this subpart apply— (i) Only if the construction work is, or reasonably can be foreseen to be, performed at a particular site so that wage rates can be determined for the locality, and only to construction work that is performed by laborers and mechanics at the site of the work;

statement: The subpart applies to construction work in a nonconstruction contract if listed conditions are met, the first being that the construction work is to be performed on a public building or public work.
quote: The requirements of this subpart apply to construction work to be performed as part of nonconstruction contracts (supply, service, research and development, etc.) if— (i) The construction work is to be performed on a public building or public work;

statement: One listed condition for construction work in a nonconstruction contract is that the contract contains specific requirements for a substantial amount of construction work exceeding the monetary threshold for application of the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute.
quote: (ii) The contract contains specific requirements for a substantial amount of construction work exceeding the monetary threshold for application of the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute
note: The printed paragraph refers to the monetary threshold without stating its amount; the amount the statute sets is printed in the section on the statute.

statement: A general wage determination contains prevailing wage rates for the types of construction it designates and is used in contracts performed within a specified geographical area.
quote: (1) A general wage determination contains prevailing wage rates for the types of construction designated in the determination, and is used in contracts performed within a specified geographical area.

statement: A general wage determination, once incorporated in a contract, normally remains effective for the life of the contract unless the contracting officer exercises an option to extend the term, and general wage determinations shall be used whenever possible.
quote: Once incorporated in a contract, a general wage determination normally remains effective for the life of the contract, unless the contracting officer exercises an option to extend the term of the contract (see 22.404-12). These determinations shall be used whenever possible.
note: The printed text cross-refers to the section on option labor standards.

statement: A project wage determination is issued at the specific request of a contracting agency, is used only when no general wage determination applies, and is effective for 180 calendar days from the date of the determination.
quote: (b) Project wage determinations. A project wage determination is issued at the specific request of a contracting agency. It is used only when no general wage determination applies, and is effective for 180 calendar days from the date of the determination.

statement: If a general wage determination applicable to the project is on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov website, the agency may use it without notifying the Department of Labor, and when necessary a request for one may be made by submitting Standard Form 308.
quote: If there is a general wage determination on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov website applicable to the project, the agency may use it without notifying the Department of Labor. When necessary, a request for a general wage determination may be made by submitting Standard Form (SF) 308,

statement: If a general wage determination is not available on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov website, a contracting agency shall submit requests for project wage determinations on Standard Form 308 to the Department of Labor.
quote: (b) Project wage determinations. If a general wage determination is not available on Wage Determinations at SAM.gov, a contracting agency shall submit requests for project wage determinations on SF 308 to the Department of Labor.

statement: Agencies should submit requests for project wage determinations for the primary site of the work to the Department of Labor at least 45 days, or 60 days if possible, before issuing the solicitation or exercising an option to extend the term of a contract.
quote: Accordingly, agencies should submit requests for project wage determinations for the primary site of the work to the Department of Labor at least 45 days (60 days if possible) before issuing the solicitation or exercising an option to extend the term of a contract.

statement: In sealed bidding, if a project wage determination for the primary site of the work expires before bid opening, or it appears before bid opening that one may expire before award, the contracting officer shall request a new determination.
quote: contracting by sealed bidding: (1) If a project wage determination for the primary site of the work expires before bid opening, or if it appears before bid opening that a project wage determination may expire before award, the contracting officer shall request a new determination

statement: One listed sealed-bidding step is that, if a project wage determination for the primary site of the work expires after bid opening but before award, the contracting officer shall request an extension of its expiration date from the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division.
quote: (2) If a project wage determination for the primary site of the work expires after bid opening but before award, the contracting officer shall request an extension of the project wage determination expiration date from the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division.

statement: In contracting by negotiation, if a project wage determination will or does expire before contract award, the contracting officer shall request a new wage determination from the Department of Labor.
quote: (c) The following procedure applies when contracting by negotiation: (1) If a project wage determination will or does expire before contract award, the contracting officer shall request a new wage determination from the Department of Labor.

statement: In sealed bidding, a written action modifying a wage determination is effective if the contracting agency receives it, or it is published on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov website, 10 or more calendar days before the date of bid opening.
quote: (b) The following applies when contracting by sealed bidding: (1) A written action modifying a wage determination shall be effective if: (i) It is received by the contracting agency, or is published on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov, 10 or more calendar days before the date of bid opening;

statement: The remaining listed items of particular attention are fringe benefits payments, hours worked, deductions, and disproportionate employment ratios of laborers, apprentices, or trainees to journeymen.
quote: (ii) Fringe benefits payments; (iii) Hours worked; (iv) Deductions; and (v) Disproportionate employment ratios of laborers, apprentices, or trainees, to journeymen.

statement: One listed sealed-bidding rule is that, if award is not made within 90 days after bid opening, a modification to a general wage determination published before award is effective for any resultant contract unless an extension of the 90-day period is obtained.
quote: (6) If an award is not made within 90 days after bid opening, any modification to a general wage determination which is published on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov before award, shall be effective for any resultant contract unless an extension of the 90-day period is obtained
note: This is the exception that the paragraph on modifications received after bid opening points to.

statement: If an effective modification is received by the contracting officer after award, the contracting officer shall modify the contract to incorporate it retroactive to the date of award and equitably adjust the contract price.
quote: (5) If an effective modification is received by the contracting officer after award, the contracting officer shall modify the contract to incorporate the wage modification retroactive to the date of award and equitably adjust the contract price

statement: A written notification by the Department of Labor that a solicitation includes the wrong wage determination or the wrong rate schedule is effective immediately, without regard to the section on modifications, if the contracting officer receives it before award.
quote: (a) The following written notifications by the Department of Labor shall be effective immediately without regard to 22.404-6 if received by the contracting officer prior to award: (1) A solicitation includes the wrong wage determination or the wrong rate schedule;

statement: In negotiated acquisitions, the contracting officer shall delay award if necessary and process the notification of an improper wage determination for the primary site of the work in the manner prescribed for a new wage determination.
quote: (c) In negotiated acquisitions, the contracting officer shall delay award, if necessary, and process the notification of an improper wage determination for the primary site of the work in the manner prescribed for a new wage determination at 22.404-5(c)(3).

statement: Each time the contracting officer exercises an option to extend the term of a construction contract, or of a contract that includes substantial and segregable construction work, the contracting officer must modify the contract to incorporate the most current wage determination.
quote: (a) Each time the contracting officer exercises an option to extend the term of a contract for construction, or a contract that includes substantial and segregable construction work, the contracting officer must modify the contract to incorporate the most current wage determination.

statement: The contracting officer must include in fixed-price contracts a clause that specifies one of the listed methods, suitable to the interest of the Government, to provide an allowance for increases or decreases in labor costs.
quote: (c) The contracting officer must include in fixed-price contracts a clause that specifies one of the following methods, suitable to the interest of the Government, to provide an allowance for any increases or decreases in labor costs

statement: One listed price adjustment method requires the contracting officer to insert 50 percent as the estimated portion of the contract price that is labor, unless the contracting officer determines before issuing the solicitation that a different percentage is more appropriate for a particular contract or requirement.
quote: The contracting officer must insert 50 percent as the estimated portion of the contract price that is labor unless the contracting officer determines, prior to issuance of the solicitation, that a different percentage is more appropriate for a particular contract or requirement.

statement: All questions about the application and interpretation of wage determinations, including their classifications, and about the interpretation of the Department of Labor regulations in the subsection that lists them are referred to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division.
quote: (c) Refer all questions relating to the application and interpretation of wage determinations (including the classifications therein) and the interpretation of the Department of Labor regulations in this subsection to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division.

statement: In computing wages paid to a laborer or mechanic, the contractor may include only listed items, the first being amounts paid in cash or deducted from payments under the conditions in 29 CFR 3.5.
quote: (a) In computing wages paid to a laborer or mechanic, the contractor may include only the following items: (1) Amounts paid in cash to the laborer or mechanic, or deducted from payments under the conditions set forth in 29 CFR 3.5.

statement: In computing required overtime payments, the contractor shall use the basic hourly rate in the wage determination, or the basic hourly rate actually paid by the contractor if higher.
quote: (c) In computing required overtime payments, (i.e., 11⁄2 times the basic hourly rate of pay) the contractor shall use the basic hourly rate of pay in the wage determination, or the basic hourly rate actually paid by the contractor, if higher.

statement: Where a laborer or mechanic is to be employed in a classification not listed in the wage determination applicable to the contract, the contracting officer shall, pursuant to the clause at 52.222-6, require the contractor to submit Standard Form 1444.
quote: to be employed in a classification that is not listed in the wage determination applicable to the contract, the contracting officer, pursuant to the clause at 52.222-6, Construction Wage Rate Requirements, shall require that the contractor submit to the contracting officer, Standard Form (SF) 1444

statement: The contracting officer shall review the request to determine whether it meets listed criteria, the first being that the classification is appropriate and its work is not performed by any classification contained in the applicable wage determination.
quote: the contracting officer shall review the request to determine whether it meets the following criteria: (1) The classification is appropriate and the work to be performed by the classification is not performed by any classification contained in the applicable wage determination.

statement: Two further listed criteria are that the classification is used in the area by the construction industry and that the proposed wage rate, including fringe benefits, bears a reasonable relationship to the wage rates in the contract's wage determination.
quote: (2) The classification is utilized in the area by the construction industry. (3) The proposed wage rate, including any fringe benefits, bears a reasonable relationship to the wage rates in the wage determination in the contract.

statement: One listed route applies where the criteria are met, the contractor and the affected laborers or mechanics or their representatives agree to the proposed classification, and the contracting officer approves.
quote: (c) (1) If the criteria in paragraph (b) of this section are met and the contractor and the laborers or mechanics to be employed in the additional classification (if known) or their representatives agree to the proposed additional classification, and the contracting officer approves,

statement: One listed step is that within 30 days of receiving the report, the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, will complete action and advise the contracting officer, or will notify the contracting officer that additional time is necessary.
quote: (d) (1) Within 30 days of receipt of the report, the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, will complete action and so advise the contracting officer, or will notify the contracting officer that additional time is necessary.

statement: The contractor must submit, within 7 calendar days after the regular payment date of the payroll week covered, copies of weekly payrolls and weekly payroll statements of compliance for itself and each subcontractor.
quote: the contractor must submit or cause to be submitted, within 7 calendar days after the regular payment date of the payroll week covered, for the contractor and each subcontractor, (1) copies of weekly payrolls applicable to the contract, and (2) weekly payroll statements of compliance.

statement: The contracting officer shall examine the payrolls and payroll statements to ensure compliance with the contract and any statutory or regulatory requirements, with particular attention to the correctness of classifications and rates.
quote: The contracting officer shall examine the payrolls and payroll statements to ensure compliance with the contract and any statutory or regulatory requirements. Particular attention should be given to— (i) The correctness of classifications and rates;

statement: The contracting agency shall retain payrolls and statements of compliance for 3 years after completion of the contract and make them available when requested by the Department of Labor during that period.
quote: (d) Preservation. The contracting agency shall retain payrolls and statements of compliance for 3 years after completion of the contract and make them available when requested by the Department of Labor at any time during that period.

statement: The contracting agency is to conduct an investigation when a compliance check indicates that substantial or willful violations may have occurred or violations have not been corrected.
quote: (a) Contracting agency responsibilities. Conduct an investigation when a compliance check indicates that substantial or willful violations may have occurred or violations have not been corrected.

statement: The contractor may rebut the findings in writing within 60 days after it receives a copy of the preliminary findings.
quote: (3) (i) The contractor may rebut the findings in writing within 60 days after it receives a copy of the preliminary findings.

statement: One listed condition for a detailed enforcement report to the Administrator within 60 days after completion of the investigation is that a contractor or subcontractor underpaid by $1,000 or more.
quote: (i) The contracting officer must send a detailed enforcement report to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, within 60 days after completion of the investigation, if— (A) A contractor or subcontractor underpaid by $1,000 or more;

statement: The clauses 52.222-6 Construction Wage Rate Requirements, 52.222-7 Withholding of Funds and 52.222-8 Payrolls and Basic Records are inserted in solicitations and contracts in excess of $2,000 for construction within the United States.
quote: (a) Insert the following clauses in solicitations and contracts in excess of $2,000 for construction within the United States: (1) 52.222-6, Construction Wage Rate Requirements. (2) 52.222-7, Withholding of Funds. (3) 52.222-8, Payrolls and Basic Records.
note: The printed list continues with further clauses, which are drafted in two later claims.

statement: One listed group of items in the clause list is 52.222-9 Apprentices and Trainees, 52.222-10 Compliance with Copeland Act Requirements, 52.222-11 Subcontracts (Labor Standards) and 52.222-12 Contract Termination—Debarment.
quote: (4) 52.222-9, Apprentices and Trainees. (5) 52.222-10, Compliance with Copeland Act Requirements. (6) 52.222-11, Subcontracts (Labor Standards). (7) 52.222-12, Contract Termination—Debarment.

statement: The clause at 52.222-16, Approval of Wage Rates, is inserted in solicitations and contracts in excess of $2,000 for cost-reimbursement construction to be performed within the United States, except for contracts with a State or political subdivision.
quote: (b) Insert the clause at 52.222-16, Approval of Wage Rates, in solicitations and contracts in excess of $2,000 for cost-reimbursement construction to be performed within the United States, except for contracts with a State or political subdivision thereof.

statement: One listed group of items in the clause list is 52.222-13 Compliance with Construction Wage Rate Requirements and Related Regulations, 52.222-14 Disputes Concerning Labor Standards and 52.222-15 Certification of Eligibility.
quote: (8) 52.222-13, Compliance with Construction Wage Rate Requirements and Related Regulations. (9) 52.222-14, Disputes Concerning Labor Standards. (10) 52.222-15, Certification of Eligibility.

statement: In one listed case, the contracting officer shall submit a report, including a copy of Standard Form 1444, of that action to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, for approval, modification, or disapproval of the additional classification and wage rate.
quote: the contracting officer shall submit a report (including a copy of SF 1444) of that action to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, for approval, modification, or disapproval of the additional classification and wage rate (including any amount designated for fringe benefits);
note: The printed paragraph continues with a second case where the parties do not agree or the criteria are not met.

statement: The provision at 52.222-5, Construction Wage Rate Requirements, Secondary Site of the Work, is inserted in solicitations in excess of $2,000 for construction within the United States.
quote: (h) Insert the provision at 52.222-5, Construction Wage Rate Requirements—Secondary Site of the Work, in solicitations in excess of $2,000 for construction within the United States.

statement: Disputes concerning the labor standards requirements of the contract are handled under the contract clause at 52.222-14 and not under the clause at 52.233-1.
quote: (1) Disputes concerning the labor standards requirements of the contract are handled under the contract clause at 52.222-14, Disputes Concerning Labor Standards, and not under the clause at 52.233-1, Disputes.

statement: The FAR defines an affirmative action program as a contractor's program that complies with Department of Labor regulations to ensure equal opportunity in employment to minorities and women.
quote: Affirmative action program means a contractor's program that complies with Department of Labor regulations to ensure equal opportunity in employment to minorities and women.

statement: The FAR defines a compliance evaluation as any one or combination of actions that the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs may take to examine a Federal contractor's compliance with one or more of the requirements of E.O. 11246.
quote: Compliance evaluation means any one or combination of actions that the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) may take to examine a Federal contractor's compliance with one or more of the requirements of E.O. 11246.

statement: The FAR defines E.O. 11246 as Parts II and IV of Executive Order 11246 of September 24, 1965, and any Executive order amending or superseding it.
quote: E.O. 11246 means Parts II and IV of Executive Order 11246, September 24, 1965 (30 FR 12319), and any Executive order amending or superseding this order (see 22.802).
note: The printed definition continues past this quote.

statement: Executive Order 11246, as amended, sets forth the Equal Opportunity clause and requires all agencies to include that clause in all nonexempt contracts and subcontracts.
quote: (a) Executive Order 11246, as amended, sets forth the Equal Opportunity clause and requires that all agencies— (1) Include this clause in all nonexempt contracts and subcontracts (see 22.807); and

statement: One listed requirement is that agencies act to ensure compliance with the Equal Opportunity clause and the Secretary of Labor's regulations to promote the full realization of equal employment opportunity for all persons, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin.
quote: (2) Act to ensure compliance with the clause and the regulations of the Secretary of Labor— (i) To promote the full realization of equal employment opportunity for all persons, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin; and
note: The next listed requirement, on compensation discussions, is not quoted.

statement: No contract or modification involving new acquisition shall be entered into, and no subcontract shall be approved by a contracting officer, with a person found ineligible by the Deputy Assistant Secretary for noncompliance with the requirements of E.O. 11246.
quote: No contract or modification involving new acquisition shall be entered into, and no subcontract shall be approved by a contracting officer, with a person who has been found ineligible by the Deputy Assistant Secretary for reasons of noncompliance with the requirements of E.O. 11246.

statement: Each agency shall maintain a listing of covered geographical areas that are subject to affirmative action requirements that specify goals for minorities and women in covered construction trades.
quote: (b) Each agency shall maintain a listing of covered geographical areas that are subject to affirmative action requirements that specify goals for minorities and women in covered construction trades.

statement: The paragraph on preaward clearances is headed as covering contracts and subcontracts of $10 million or more, excluding construction.
quote: (a) Preaward clearances for contracts and subcontracts of $10 million or more (excluding construction).

statement: Except as provided in the paragraphs it names, if the estimated amount of the contract or subcontract is $10 million or more, the contracting officer shall request clearance from the appropriate OFCCP regional office before the events listed next.
quote: (1) Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(4) and (a)(8) of this section, if the estimated amount of the contract or subcontract is $10 million or more, the contracting officer shall request clearance from the appropriate OFCCP regional office before—

statement: One listed event is award of any contract, including any indefinite delivery contract or letter contract, and another listed event is modification of an existing contract for new effort that would constitute a contract award.

quote: (2) Facsimile, email, and scanned documents are not acceptable electronic forms of payment requests or receiving reports.

statement: Only one type of financing will be included in the resultant contract, except as may be authorized on separate orders subject to FAR 32.1003(c).
quote: Only one type of financing will be included in the resultant contract, except as may be authorized on separate orders subject to FAR 32.1003(c)).

statement: The contracting officer shall analyze the performance-based payment schedule using the performance-based payments (PBP) analysis tool.
quote: (ii) The contracting officer shall analyze the performance-based payment schedule using the performance-based payments (PBP) analysis tool.

quote: (iii) The contracting officer shall document in the contract file that the performance-based payment schedule provides a mutually beneficial settlement position that reflects adequate consideration to the Government for the improved contractor cash flow.

statement: When considering performance-based payments, the DFARS says to obtain from the offeror or contractor a proposed performance-based payments schedule that includes all performance-based payments events, completion criteria and event values along with the projected monthly expenditure profile.
quote: (A) When considering performance-based payments, obtain from the offeror/contractor a proposed performance-based payments schedule that includes all performance-based payments events, completion criteria and event values along with the projected monthly expenditure profile

statement: If the contract contains foreign military sales requirements, the contracting officer shall provide instructions for distribution of the contract financing payments to each country's account.
quote: (c) Instructions for multiple appropriations. If the contract contains foreign military sales requirements, the contracting officer shall provide instructions for distribution of the contract financing payments to each country's account.

statement: The temporary alternative method of submission is provided for in the contract administration data section of the contract or task or delivery order.
quote: for a temporary alternative method of submission of payment requests and receiving reports in the contract administration data section of the contract or task or delivery order

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a contract financing payment as an authorized Government disbursement of monies to a contractor prior to acceptance of supplies or services by the Government.
quote: Contract financing payment means an authorized Government disbursement of monies to a contractor prior to acceptance of supplies or services by the Government.

statement: FAR 32.001 lists advance payments, performance-based payments, commercial advance and interim payments, and progress payments based on cost under the Progress Payments clause among the contract financing payments.
quote: (1) Contract financing payments include— (i) Advance payments; (ii) Performance-based payments; (iii) Commercial advance and interim payments; (iv) Progress payments based on cost under the clause at 52.232-16, Progress Payments;
note: The printed list also includes progress payments based on a percentage or stage of completion and interim payments under a cost reimbursement contract, which later claims state with their exceptions.

statement: FAR 32.001 says contract financing payments do not include invoice payments, payments for partial deliveries, or lease and rental payments.
quote: (2) Contract financing payments do not include— (i) Invoice payments; (ii) Payments for partial deliveries; or (iii) Lease and rental payments.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines liquidate as decreasing a payment for an accepted supply item or service under a contract to recoup financing payments previously paid to the contractor, and defines unusual contract financing as any financing not deemed customary contract financing by the agency.
quote: Liquidate means to decrease a payment for an accepted supply item or service under a contract for the purpose of recouping financing payments previously paid to the contractor. Unusual contract financing means any financing not deemed customary contract financing by the agency.

statement: FAR 32.001 defines the designated payment office as the office designated in the contract to make invoice payments or contract financing payments, which will normally be the Government disbursing office, and defines the due date as the date on which payment should be made.
quote: Designated payment office means the office designated in the contract to make invoice payments or contract financing payments. Normally, this will be the Government disbursing office. Due date means the date on which payment should be made.

statement: FAR 32.007 sets the due date for contract financing payments by the designated payment office at the 30th day after the designated billing office receives a proper contract financing request, unless otherwise prescribed in agency policies and procedures or otherwise specified in paragraph (b) of that section.
quote: Unless otherwise prescribed in agency policies and procedures or otherwise specified in paragraph (b) of this section, the due date for making contract financing payments by the designated payment office is the 30th day after the designated billing office receives a proper contract financing request

statement: FAR 32.007 says that if an audit or other review of a specific financing request is required to ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of the contract, the designated payment office is not compelled to make payment by the specified due date.
quote: (2) If an audit or other review of a specific financing request is required to ensure compliance with the terms and conditions of the contract, the designated payment office is not compelled to make payment by the specified due date.

statement: FAR 32.007 gives as an example that a shorter period may be justified by an agency if the nature and extent of contract financing arrangements are integrated with agency contract pricing policies, and says agency heads must not prescribe a period shorter than 7 days or longer than 30 days.
quote: For example, a shorter period may be justified by an agency if the nature and extent of contract financing arrangements are integrated with agency contract pricing policies. (4) Agency heads must not prescribe a period shorter than 7 days or longer than 30 days.

statement: FAR 32.007 says that for advance payments, loans, or other arrangements that do not involve recurrent submission of contract financing requests, the designated payment office will make payment in accordance with the applicable contract financing terms or as directed by the contracting officer.
quote: (b) For advance payments, loans, or other arrangements that do not involve recurrent submission of contract financing requests, the designated payment office will make payment in accordance with the applicable contract financing terms or as directed by the contracting officer.

statement: FAR 32.007 says the Government will not pay an interest penalty to the contractor as a result of delayed contract financing payments.
quote: (e) The Government will not pay an interest penalty to the contractor as a result of delayed contract financing payments.

statement: FAR 32.102 describes advance payments as advances of money by the Government to a prime contractor before, in anticipation of, and for the purpose of complete performance under one or more contracts.
quote: (a) Advance payments are advances of money by the Government to a prime contractor before, in anticipation of, and for the purpose of complete performance under one or more contracts.

statement: FAR 32.102 describes progress payments based on costs as made on the basis of costs incurred by the contractor as work progresses under the contract.
quote: (b) Progress payments based on costs are made on the basis of costs incurred by the contractor as work progresses under the contract.

statement: FAR 32.102 describes loan guarantees as made by Federal Reserve banks, on behalf of designated guaranteeing agencies, to enable contractors to obtain financing from private sources under contracts for the acquisition of supplies or services for the national defense.
quote: (c) Loan guarantees are made by Federal Reserve banks, on behalf of designated guaranteeing agencies, to enable contractors to obtain financing from private sources under contracts for the acquisition of supplies or services for the national defense.

statement: FAR 32.102 describes performance-based payments as contract financing payments made on the basis of performance measured by objective, quantifiable methods, accomplishment of defined events, or other quantifiable measures of results.
quote: (f) Performance-based payments are contract financing payments made on the basis of— (1) Performance measured by objective, quantifiable methods; (2) Accomplishment of defined events; or (3) Other quantifiable measures of results.

statement: FAR 32.111(a) says the contracting officer shall insert the listed clauses, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates, in accordance with agency regulations.
quote: (a) The contracting officer shall insert the following clauses, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates, in accordance with agency regulations—

quote: (1) The clause at 52.232-1, Payments, in solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract, a fixed-price service contract, or a contract for nonregulated communication services is contemplated;

quote: 52.232-2, Payment under Fixed-Price Research and Development Contracts, in solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price research and development contract is contemplated; (3) The clause at 52.232-3, Payments under Personal Services Contracts, in solicitations and contracts for personal services;

statement: One clause listed in FAR 32.111(a) is 52.232-4, Payments under Transportation Contracts and Transportation-Related Services Contracts, for solicitations and contracts for transportation or transportation-related services.
quote: (4) The clause at 52.232-4, Payments under Transportation Contracts and Transportation-Related Services Contracts, in solicitations and contracts for transportation or transportation-related services;

statement: One clause listed in FAR 32.111(a) is 52.232-5, Payments under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, for solicitations and contracts for construction when a fixed-price contract is contemplated.
quote: (5) The clause at 52.232-5, Payments under Fixed-Price Construction Contracts, in solicitations and contracts for construction when a fixed-price contract is contemplated;

statement: One clause listed in FAR 32.111(a) is 52.232-6, Payments under Communication Service Contracts with Common Carriers, for solicitations and contracts for regulated communication services by common carriers.
quote: (6) The clause at 52.232-6, Payments under Communication Service Contracts with Common Carriers, in solicitations and contracts for regulated communication services by common carriers;

statement: One clause listed in FAR 32.111(a) is 52.232-7, Payments under Time-and-Materials and Labor-Hour Contracts, for solicitations and contracts when a time-and-materials or labor-hour contract is contemplated.
quote: (7) The clause at 52.232-7, Payments under Time-and-Materials and Labor-Hour Contracts, in solicitations and contracts when a time-and-materials or labor-hour contract is contemplated.

statement: FAR 32.111(c) says the contracting officer shall insert the clause at 52.232-10, Payments under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts, in fixed-price architect-engineer contracts, appropriately modified with respect to payment due dates in accordance with agency regulations.
quote: (c) The contracting officer shall insert the following clauses, appropriately modified with respect to payments due dates in accordance with agency regulations: (1) The clause at 52.232-10, Payments under Fixed-Price Architect-Engineer Contracts, in fixed-price architect-engineer contracts.

statement: One clause listed in FAR 32.111(c) is 52.232-11, Extras, for solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract, fixed-price service contract, or a transportation contract is contemplated.
quote: (2) The clause at 52.232-11, Extras, in solicitations and contracts when a fixed-price supply contract, fixed-price service contract, or a transportation contract is contemplated.

statement: FAR 32.304-5 says the agency shall generally require a contractor that is provided a guaranteed loan to execute an assignment of claims under defense production contracts, including any contracts entered into during the term of the guaranteed loan that are eligible for financing under the loan.
quote: The agency shall generally require a contractor that is provided a guaranteed loan to execute an assignment of claims under defense production contracts (including any contracts entered into during the term of the guaranteed loan that are eligible for financing under the loan)

statement: FAR 32.304-5 says the agency need not require assignment if any of the listed conditions is present, and one listed condition is that the contractor's financial condition is so strong that the protection to the Government provided by an assignment of claims is unnecessary.
quote: however, the agency need not require assignment if any of the following conditions are present: (1) The contractor's financial condition is so strong that the protection to the Government provided by an assignment of claims is unnecessary.

statement: FAR 32.403 says advance payments may be considered useful and appropriate for the listed cases, two of which are contracts for experimental, research, or development work with nonprofit educational or research institutions and contracts solely for the management and operation of Government-owned plants.
quote: Advance payments may be considered useful and appropriate for the following: (a) Contracts for experimental, research, or development work with nonprofit educational or research institutions. (b) Contracts solely for the management and operation of Government-owned plants.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says to insert the clause at 52.232-16, Progress Payments, in solicitations that may result in contracts providing for progress payments based on costs and in fixed-price contracts under which the Government will provide progress payments based on costs.
quote: (a) (1) Insert the clause at 52.232-16, Progress Payments, in— (i) Solicitations that may result in contracts providing for progress payments based on costs; and (ii) Fixed-price contracts under which the Government will provide progress payments based on costs.

statement: FAR 32.502-4 says to use the clause with its Alternate I if the contractor is a small business concern and with its Alternate II if the contract is a letter contract.
quote: (b) If the contractor is a small business concern, use the clause with its Alternate I. (c) If the contract is a letter contract, use the clause with its Alternate II.
note: The clause meant here is the Progress Payments clause that paragraph (a)(1) of the same section says to insert.

note: The clause meant here is the Progress Payments clause that paragraph (a)(1) of the same section says to insert.

statement: FAR 32.503-2 says the extent of progress payments supervision, by prepayment review or periodic review, should vary inversely with the contractor's experience, performance record, reliability, quality of management, and financial strength, and with the adequacy of the contractor's accounting system and controls.
quote: (a) The extent of progress payments supervision, by prepayment review or periodic review, should vary inversely with the contractor's experience, performance record, reliability, quality of management, and financial strength, and with the adequacy of the contractor's accounting system and controls.

statement: FAR 32.503-2 says the administering office must keep itself informed of the contractor's overall operations and financial condition.
quote: (b) The administering office must keep itself informed of the contractor's overall operations and financial condition

statement: FAR 32.601 defines contract debts as amounts that have been paid to a contractor to which the contractor is not currently entitled under the terms and conditions of the contract, or that are otherwise due from the contractor under the terms and conditions of the contract.
quote: (a) Contract debts are amounts that— (1) Have been paid to a contractor to which the contractor is not currently entitled under the terms and conditions of the contract; or (2) Are otherwise due from the contractor under the terms and conditions of the contract.

statement: FAR 32.1103 says the Government shall provide all contract payments through EFT except in the listed cases, one of which is that the office making payment under a contract that requires payment by EFT loses the ability to release payment by EFT.
quote: The Government shall provide all contract payments through EFT except if— (a) The office making payment under a contract that requires payment by EFT, loses the ability to release payment by EFT.

statement: Two further listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are a payment to be received by or on behalf of the contractor outside the United States and Puerto Rico and a contract paid in other than United States currency, each marked in the text with a cross-reference to 32.1106(b).
quote: (b) The payment is to be received by or on behalf of the contractor outside the United States and Puerto Rico (but see 32.1106(b)); (c) A contract is paid in other than United States currency (but see 32.1106(b));

statement: A further listed exception in FAR 32.1103 is payment by EFT under a classified contract that could compromise the safeguarding of classified information or national security, or for which arrangements for appropriate EFT payments would be impractical due to security considerations.
quote: (d) Payment by EFT under a classified contract could compromise the safeguarding of classified information or national security, or arrangements for appropriate EFT payments would be impractical due to security considerations;

statement: One situation named in the exception for deployed and emergency operations in FAR 32.1103 is a contract awarded by a deployed contracting officer in the course of military operations, including, but not limited to, contingency operations as defined in 2.101.

note: The paragraph attaches the conditions on EFT possibility and operation objectives after both situations; they are stated in the next claim.

statement: Two further listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are that the agency does not expect to make more than one payment to the same recipient within a one-year period, and that the agency's need for supplies and services is of such unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT.
quote: (f) The agency does not expect to make more than one payment to the same recipient within a one-year period; (g) An agency's need for supplies and services is of such unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT;

statement: The last two listed exceptions in FAR 32.1103 are that there is only one source for supplies and services and the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT, and that EFT is otherwise not required where authorized by Department of the Treasury Regulations at 31 CFR part 208.
quote: (h) There is only one source for supplies and services and the Government would be seriously injured unless payment is made by a method other than EFT; or (i) Otherwise authorized by Department of the Treasury Regulations at 31 CFR part 208.

statement: FAR 32.1108 says a Governmentwide commercial purchase card charge authorizes the third party that issued the card to make immediate payment to the contractor, and that the Government reimburses the third party at a later date.
quote: A Governmentwide commercial purchase card charge authorizes the third party (e.g., financial institution) that issued the purchase card to make immediate payment to the contractor. The Government reimburses the third party at a later date for the third party's payment to the contractor.

statement: FAR 32.1108 says the contracting officer shall not authorize the Governmentwide commercial purchase card as a method of payment during any period the SAM indicates that the contractor has delinquent debt subject to collection under the TOP.

statement: FAR 32.1110(a)(2)(i) lists the clause at 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, for solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment.
quote: (2) (i) 52.232-34, Payment by Electronic Funds Transfer—Other than System for Award Management, in solicitations and contracts that require EFT as the method for payment

quote: but do not include the provision at 52.204-7, System for Award Management, or a similar agency clause that requires the contractor to be registered in SAM.

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information.
quote: (c) If EFT information is to be submitted to other than the payment office in accordance with agency procedures, the contracting officer shall insert in solicitations and contracts the clause at 52.232-35, Designation of Office for Government Receipt of Electronic Funds Transfer Information,

statement: FAR 32.1110 says that if the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert in the solicitation and contract or agreement the clause at 52.232-37.
quote: (e) If the contract or agreement provides for the use of delivery orders, and provides that the ordering office designate the method of payment for individual orders, the contracting officer shall insert, in the solicitation and contract or agreement, the clause at 52.232-37,

quote: Delivery payment means a payment for accepted supplies or services, including payments for accepted partial deliveries. Commercial financing payments are liquidated by deduction from these payments. Delivery payments are invoice payments for prompt payment purposes.

quote: Invoice payment means a Government disbursement of monies to a contractor under a contract or other authorization for supplies or services accepted by the Government.

quote: (1) Invoice payments include— (i) Payments for partial deliveries that have been accepted by the Government; (ii) Final cost or fee payments where amounts owed have been settled between the Government and the contractor;

statement: FAR 32.001 defines a commercial interim payment as any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment, and says these payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes.
quote: Commercial interim payment means any payment that is not a commercial advance payment or a delivery payment. These payments are contract financing payments for prompt payment purposes

statement: FAR 32.001 defines the designated billing office as the office or person, governmental or nongovernmental, designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.
quote: Designated billing office means the office or person (governmental or nongovernmental) designated in the contract where the contractor first submits invoices and contract financing requests.

statement: FAR 32.007 says agency heads may prescribe shorter periods for payment of contract financing based on contract pricing or administrative considerations.

statement: FAR 32.111(a)(7), in the prescription for the clause at 52.232-7 for time-and-materials and labor-hour contracts, says that, if the contracting officer determines it is necessary to withhold payment to protect the Government interests, paragraph (a)(7) of that clause permits the contracting officer to unilaterally issue a modification requiring the contractor to withhold 5 percent of amounts due.

statement: DFARS 204.7103-2 says to follow the procedures at PGI 204.7103-2 for numbering contract line items.

quote: Follow the procedures at PGI 204.7108 for inclusion of payment instructions in contracts.

quote: (b) All subline items and exhibit line items under one contract line item shall be the same contract type as the contract line item.
