quote: When designating the internal organization responsible for managing the program efforts, the contractor must assign a program manager with sufficient authority and responsibility to ensure the performance of the authorized work.

statement: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.
quote: The manager assigned to subcontractor work must have full responsibility for the authorized work.

statement: The organizational breakdown structure is defined with uniquely defined nomenclature.

statement: The section opened for this topic is the guide's organization guideline on integrating the work breakdown structure and the organizational structure, labelled in the source as an EIA standard guideline.

statement: The guideline requires the contractor to integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.
quote: Integrate the program work breakdown structure and organizational structure to identify management control points where responsibility is assigned to specific work scope.

quote: The intersection of the lowest level WBS element and the OBS is the point at which control account(s) are established.

statement: Control accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single work breakdown structure level across the program.
quote: Control Accounts should not be arbitrarily established at a single WBS level across the program.

quote: Each control account has a corresponding Control Account Manager (CAM), who is responsible for ensuring the accomplishment of work in the control account and is the focal point of management control.

statement: For management control purposes there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single work breakdown structure element, or multiple control accounts within one organizational element, driven by scope and exit criteria.
quote: For management control purposes, there may be one or more responsible organizations supporting a single WBS or multiple control accounts within one OBS element driven by scope and exit criteria

statement: For scope that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a summary level planning package above the control account level with an assigned manager.

statement: Schedule margin, if used, is identifiable, derived from a risk management approach, and justifiable in duration; it may only be represented in the schedule as the last task before key contractual events, significant logical integration/test milestones, end item deliverables, and/or contract completion.
quote: Schedule margin, if used, is identifiable, derived from a risk management approach, justifiable in duration, and may only be represented in the schedule as the last task before key contractual events, significant logical integration/test milestones, end item deliverables, and/or contract completion.

statement: The seventh earned value guideline requires establishing and maintaining a time-phased budget baseline comprised of scope, schedule, and budget at the control account level, although budget for far-term efforts may be held in higher-level accounts until an appropriate time for allocation at the control account level.
quote: Establish and maintain a time-phased budget baseline comprised of scope, schedule, and budget at the control account level. Budget for far-term efforts may be held in higher-level accounts until an appropriate time for allocation at the control account level.

statement: The Performance Measurement Baseline is the time-phased budget plan against which actual performance is assessed.
quote: The PMB is the time-phased budget plan against which actual performance is assessed.

statement: For future effort that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish a Summary Level Planning Package above the control account level.
quote: For future effort that cannot practically be identified to a control account, it is permissible to establish an SLPP above the control account level.

statement: Budget set aside for known and unforeseen program risks and contingencies is referred to as Management Reserve and is not included in the Performance Measurement Baseline.
quote: The budget set aside for known and unforeseen program risks and contingencies is referred to as Management Reserve (MR) and is not included in the PMB

statement: When Total Allocated Budget exceeds the Contract Budget Base, an Over Target Baseline occurs.
quote: When the Total Allocated Budget (TAB) exceeds the CBB, an Over Target Baseline (OTB) occurs.

statement: When the baseline schedule exceeds contract milestones, an Over Target Schedule occurs.
quote: When the baseline schedule exceeds contract milestones, an Over Target Schedule (OTS) occurs

statement: The Performance Measurement Baseline is time-phased in alignment with the Integrated Master Schedule, with budget distributed in accordance with the accounting calendar for authorized work scope including control accounts and summary level planning packages.
quote: The PMB is time-phased in alignment with the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), with budget distributed in accordance with the accounting calendar for the authorized work scope including all control accounts and SLPPs.

statement: The eighth earned value guideline requires authorizing control account scope, schedule, and budget comprised of elements of cost, such as labor, material, and subcontractors, required to complete the effort.
quote: Authorize control account scope, schedule, and budget comprised of elements of cost (labor, material, subcontractors, etc.) required to complete the effort.

statement: Approved work authorization precedes the baseline start and actual start of work.
quote: Approved work authorization precedes the baseline start and actual start of work.

statement: Budgets are established by element of cost: direct labor, subcontractor, material, and other direct costs.
quote: Budgets are established by EOC: direct labor, subcontractor, material, and other direct costs

statement: Current rates are to be utilized when incorporating new scope into the Performance Measurement Baseline.
quote: Current rates are to be utilized when incorporating new scope into the PMB.

statement: Descoped work is to be removed using the rates that are baselined with the affected scope.
quote: Descoped work is to be removed using the rates that are baselined with the affected scope

statement: The budget for authorized subcontractor work is based initially on the prime contractor's estimated value.
quote: The budget for authorized subcontractor work is based initially on the prime contractor’s estimated value

statement: The ninth earned value guideline requires planning authorized scope, schedule, and budget into work packages and planning packages.
quote: Plan the authorized scope, schedule, and budget into work packages and/or planning packages.

statement: Budgets are determined in terms of dollars, hours, or other measurable units such that the sum of all work package and planning package budgets equals the control account budget.
quote: Determine budgets in terms of dollars, hours, or other measurable units such that the sum of all work package and planning package budgets equal the control account budget.

statement: Work packages reflect the expected way the work is to be done and are a distinguishable subdivision of a control account, assignable to a single program organizational element.
quote: Work packages reflect the expected way the work is to be done and are a distinguishable subdivision of a control account, assignable to a single program organizational element.

statement: Distributing all control account budgets to either work packages or planning packages ensures the Performance Measurement Baseline is planned at an executable level that aligns with how meaningful performance measurements will be achieved.
quote: Distributing all control account budgets to either work packages or planning packages ensures the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) is planned at an executable level that aligns with how meaningful performance measurements will be achieved.

statement: When authorized control account work scope cannot be planned in the near-term, a planning package is used for holding scope, schedule, and budget until the work is detail planned into work packages.
quote: When authorized control account work scope cannot be planned in the near-term, a planning package is used for holding the scope, schedule, and budget until the work is detail planned into work packages.

statement: The planning package is time-phased with known schedule requirements and detail planned into work packages at the earliest practicable point before work is performed on its scope.
quote: The planning package is time-phased with the known schedule requirements and is detail planned into work package(s) at the earliest practicable point before any work is performed on the scope contained in the planning package.

statement: The sum of all work package budgets plus planning package budgets within control accounts equals the budgets authorized for those control accounts.
quote: The sum of all work package budgets plus planning package budgets within control accounts equals the budgets authorized for those control accounts.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its tenth guideline, on establishing performance measurement criteria.
quote: 3.6 GUIDELINE 10: ESTABLISH PERFORMANCE MEASUREMENT CRITERIA
note: This is guide text, not a codified FAR, DFARS or CAS section.

statement: An earned value management system establishes objective performance measurement criteria for each work package, consistent with the way the work is expected to be accomplished, and identifies only effort that is not measurable as level of effort.
quote: Establish objective performance measurement criteria for each work package consistent with the way work is expected to be accomplished. Only that effort which is not measurable is identified as level of effort.

statement: Classification of work as level of effort is limited to activities that have no practicable, measurable output or product that can be discretely planned and objectively measured at the work package level.
quote: Classification of work scope as Level of Effort (LOE) is limited to activities that have no practicable, measurable output or product associated with technical effort that can be discretely planned and objectively measured at the work package level.

statement: The control account manager assesses each assigned work package and determines whether there is a discrete way to measure progress towards its completion.
quote: The Control Account Manager assesses each assigned Work Package and determines if there is a discrete way to measure progress towards its completion.

statement: Where long-duration work packages are unavoidable, interim milestones that model measurable technical accomplishment are required for performance measurement.
quote: Where long-duration work packages are unavoidable, interim milestones modelling measurable, technical accomplishment are required for performance measurement.

statement: Apportioned effort should be used when work of a supporting nature ties directly to a discrete technical activity.
quote: The concept of "apportioned effort" should be used when work of a supporting nature ties directly to a discrete technical activity.

statement: If the contractor chooses to use apportioned effort, the system documentation must cover the requirements for the technique and must document the factor used to establish the relationship.
quote: If the contractor chooses to use this technique, the EVMS documentation must cover the requirements for the use of this measurement technique and the need to document the factor used to establish the relationship

statement: Level of effort earned value reflects only the passage of time during which those activities are planned, so it never produces a schedule variance and always equals the budgeted cost for work scheduled.
quote: The nature of LOE is such that the BCWP reflects only the passage of time during which LOE activities are planned; there is never a Schedule Variance (SV) (i.e., BCWP always equals BCWS).

statement: The method that calculates BCWP as (ACWP/EAC) x BAC requires the estimate at completion to be evaluated and updated every month.
quote: BCWP = (ACWP/EAC) x BAC. The use of this method requires that the EAC be evaluated and updated every month.

statement: Earned value for discrete material items may be claimed upon receipt, inspection and acceptance only if the items are placed into use within a reasonable time or are specifically identified to a serially numbered end item.
quote: BCWP for discrete material items may be claimed upon receipt, inspection, and acceptance, provided the material items are placed into use within a reasonable time or are specifically identified to a serially numbered end item.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its eleventh guideline, on establishing indirect budgets.
quote: 3.7 GUIDELINE 11: ESTABLISH INDIRECT BUDGETS

statement: Indirect rates developed by the responsible organizations are applied to the program’s direct resource budgets at the applicable level, which determines the indirect budgets that support the establishment of the performance measurement baseline.
quote: Apply indirect rates, developed by the responsible organizations, to the program’s direct resource budgets, at the applicable level, to determine the indirect budgets that support the establishment of the performance measurement baseline.

statement: Indirect budgets such as overhead, general and administrative cost, and cost of money are established and included in the performance measurement baseline at an appropriate level for visibility.
quote: To ensure indirect budgets (e.g., Overhead, General & Administrative, and Cost of Money) are established and included in the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) at the appropriate level for visibility.

statement: The guide treats it as critical to the contractor that, at the end of the accounting year, all indirect expenses are allocated.
quote: It is critical to the contractor that, at the end of the accounting year, all indirect expenses are allocated.

statement: Indirect budgets are established at the appropriate organizational level for each pool and cost sub-element.
quote: Indirect budgets are established at the appropriate organizational level for each pool and cost sub-element.

statement: Budgets for indirect costs on programs are developed and planned in conjunction with the direct budgets and are consistent with the contractor’s documented procedures for how indirect costs are approved and allocated to the program.
quote: Budgets for indirect costs as implemented on the programs are developed and planned in conjunction with the direct budgets and are consistent with the contractor’s documented procedures for how indirect costs are approved and allocated to the program

statement: Indirect budgets are incorporated into the baseline in concert with the described processes and current rates, which may be approved, provisional or proposed.
quote: Indirect budgets are incorporated into the PMB in concert with described processes and current rates (i.e., approved, provisional, proposed).

statement: Comparing actual indirect expenses with the established indirect budgets shows whether absorption under the existing documented allocation schemes is on track or whether allocation rates require adjustment.
quote: By comparing actual indirect expenses to established indirect budgets, the contractor can determine if the absorption of indirect expenses based on existing documented allocation schemes is on track or if allocation rates require adjustment.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its twelfth guideline, on identifying undistributed budget and management reserve.
quote: 3.8 GUIDELINE 12: IDENTIFY UNDISTRIBUTED BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT RESERVE

statement: Undistributed budget is budget that applies to specific contractual effort that has not yet been distributed to control accounts or summary level planning packages.
quote: UB is budget that applies to specific contractual effort that has not yet been distributed to control accounts or Summary Level Planning Packages (SLPPs).

statement: Undistributed budget accommodates contract situations where authorized scope and budget cannot yet be distributed within the baseline to control accounts or summary level planning packages.
quote: UB accommodates contract situations where authorized scope and budget cannot yet be distributed within the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) to control accounts or SLPPs.

statement: Undistributed budget is part of the performance measurement baseline and is budget associated with contractually authorized scope that has not yet been distributed to an organizational element at or below the reporting level.
quote: UB is part of the PMB and is budget associated with contractually authorized work scope that has not yet been distributed to an organizational element at or below the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) reporting level.

statement: Undistributed budget is a transitional budget that should be distributed in a timely manner.
quote: UB is a transitional budget that should be distributed in a timely manner.

statement: Management reserve belongs to the contractor program manager, not the Government, and provides the contractor with a budget for unplanned activities within the current program scope.
quote: MR belongs to the contractor program manager, not the Government, and provides the contractor with a budget for unplanned activities within the current program scope.

statement: Management reserve is not associated with a specific scope of work and is not included in the performance measurement baseline.
quote: MR is not associated with a specific scope of work and is not included in the PMB.

statement: Management reserve is not a contingency fund: it may not be eliminated from contract prices by the customer during later negotiations and may not be used to absorb the cost of contract changes.
quote: MR is not a contingency fund and may neither be eliminated from contract prices by the customer during subsequent negotiations nor used to absorb the cost of contract changes.

statement: Management reserve is always reported as a positive value and is set aside for program risks or unplanned events that are in scope to the contract.
quote: MR is always reported as a positive value and is set aside for program risks or unplanned events that are in-scope to the contract.

statement: Management reserve belonging to a major subcontractor is incorporated into the prime contractor’s earned value system with traceability to the subcontractor’s reported reserve.
quote: MR belonging to a major subcontractor is incorporated into the prime contractor’s EVMS with traceability to the subcontractor’s reported MR.

statement: Undistributed budget has defined scope, is separately identified, is traceable to contractual actions and is part of the baseline, while management reserve has no scope defined and is separately identified outside the baseline.
quote: UB has defined scope, is separately identified, is traceable to contractual actions, and is part of the PMB. MR has no scope defined and is separately identified outside of the PMB.
note: The guide states that undistributed budget and management reserve serve distinctly different purposes.

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its thirteenth guideline, on reconciling to target costs.
quote: 3.9 GUIDELINE 13: RECONCILE TO TARGET COSTS

statement: The program target cost goal is reconciled with the sum of all internal program budgets and management reserve.
quote: Provide that the program target cost goal is reconciled with the sum of all internal program budgets and management reserve.

statement: Contract target cost is synonymous with negotiated contract cost.
quote: Contract Target Cost is synonymous with Negotiated Contract Cost (NCC).

statement: The contract target cost plus authorized unpriced work must reconcile with the contract budget base and the total allocated budget.
quote: The Contract Target Cost plus Authorized Unpriced Work (AUW) must reconcile with the Contract Budget Base (CBB)/Total Allocated Budget (TAB).

statement: Control account budgets, summary level planning packages and undistributed budget are summed to the budget at completion of the baseline, and that sum plus management reserve equals the contract budget base.
quote: All control account budgets, SLPPs, and UB are summed up to a total value known as the Budget at Completion (BAC) of the PMB. Having validated the sum of the internal budgets, this sum plus MR equals the value known as the CBB.

statement: The contract budget base also equals the total allocated budget unless a recognized over-target baseline exists; with one, the total allocated budget equals the contract budget base plus the above target budget.
quote: The CBB also equals the TAB unless there is a recognized Over-Target Baseline (OTB). In that case, the TAB equals the CBB plus Above Target Budget (ATB) (see Guideline 27).

statement: The DoD EVMS Interpretation Guide presents this requirement as its fourteenth guideline, on assessing progress.
quote: 4.1 GUIDELINE 14: ASSESS PROGRESS

statement: Using predefined performance measurement criteria, the contractor statuses the schedule and assesses physical progress to determine the budget earned.
quote: Using predefined performance measurement criteria, status the schedule and assess physical progress to determine budget earned.

statement: Earned value for material items may not be credited earlier than the actual receipt of the material nor later than the consumption of the item.
quote: Earned value for material items may not be credited earlier than the actual receipt of the material nor later than the consumption of the item.

statement: Schedule status and the physical progress assessment are updated in accordance with the business cycle based on the size, risk and complexity of the program, but no less than monthly.
quote: Schedule status (time-based) and assessing physical progress (earned value) is updated in accordance with the business cycle based on the size, risk, and complexity of the program, but no less than monthly.

statement: Level of effort performance is earned with the passage of time without consideration if actual work is performed.
quote: Level of Effort (LOE) performance is earned with the passage of time without consideration if actual work is performed.

statement: The point at which material costs transfer from the accounting system to the earned value system as actual cost must fall within the same accounting period in which earned value for that material is claimed.
quote: the point of transfer of costs from the accounting system to the Earned Value Management System (EVMS) as actual cost for the material occurs within the same accounting period that earned value for that material is claimed.

statement: To keep the schedule integrated with the baseline, the schedule progress reporting period should align to the accounting period.
quote: To ensure integration between the IMS and the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) the schedule progress reporting period should align to the accounting period.

statement: Guideline 15 requires actual direct and indirect costs to be collected by element of cost from a formal system controlled by the general books of account, for comparison with corresponding budgets.
quote: Collect actual costs (direct and indirect), by elements of cost, from a formal system controlled by the general books of account for comparison to corresponding budgets in the EVMS.

statement: When actual costs are not available for comparison, estimated costs are entered into the EVMS.
quote: Where actual costs are not available for comparison, estimated costs will be entered into the EVMS.

statement: Indirect costs must be allocated in a consistent manner to the contracts at the level where the indirect budgets are established.
quote: ensure all indirect costs are properly and correctly allocated in a consistent manner to the contract(s) at the level where indirect budgets are established.

statement: All purchased material for which earned value has been calculated must be accounted for, including material residual to the program.
quote: Account for all purchased material for which earned value has been calculated, including material residual to the program.

statement: The material management process must reflect acquisition, issue to control accounts, return of unused material, scrap quantity and disposition, and residual material inventory.
quote: This process must reflect the acquisition, issue to control accounts, return of unused materials from control accounts, scrap quantity and disposition, and residual material inventory.

statement: Schedule variance is the comparison of the amount of planned budget and the amount of budget earned for work accomplished.
quote: Comparison of the amount of planned budget and the amount of budget earned for work accomplished. This comparison provides the schedule variance.

statement: Cost variance is the comparison of the amount of the budget earned and the actual (applied where appropriate) direct costs for the same work.
quote: Comparison of the amount of the budget earned and the actual (applied where appropriate) direct costs for the same work. This comparison provides the cost variance.

statement: Schedule and cost variance information is generated at least monthly for the control account and higher levels, as necessary for management control, using actual cost data from or reconcilable with the accounting system.
quote: At least on a monthly basis, generate the following information for the control account and higher levels, as necessary for management control, using actual cost data from or reconcilable with the accounting system

statement: A positive schedule or cost variance value indicates a favorable condition, and a negative value indicates an unfavorable condition.
quote: A positive value indicates a favorable condition, and a negative value indicates an unfavorable condition.

statement: Guideline 18 requires identifying and evaluating, at least monthly for each control account, the significant differences between planned and actual schedule and cost performance, and analyzing and providing the reasons.
quote: Identify and evaluate, at least monthly for each control account, the significant differences between both planned and actual schedule performance and planned and actual cost performance; and analyze and provide the reasons for the variances in the detail needed by program management.

statement: Analyzing deviations from the performance measurement baseline lets management implement corrective actions to regain contract objectives.
quote: The ability to analyze deviations from the established Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) permits management, at all levels, to implement corrective actions rapidly and effectively, to regain contract objectives.

statement: Schedule variance analysis is supplemented with integrated master schedule analysis and assesses the impact on future critical path, near-critical path, and driving path activities.
quote: Schedule variance analysis is supplemented with Integrated Master Schedule analysis and assesses the impact to future activities on the critical path, near-critical paths, and driving paths.

statement: Guideline 19 requires evaluating indirect cost variances and the impact of indirect cost performance on individual program performance.
quote: Evaluate indirect cost variances and the impact of indirect cost performance on individual program performance.

statement: The program's indirect cost variance is the portion of total cost variance attributed to indirect rate adjustments.
quote: The program’s indirect cost variance is the portion of the total cost variance attributed to indirect rate adjustments.

statement: Guideline 20 requires updating control account estimates at completion from variance analysis and indirect performance evaluations, and calculating the variance at completion by comparing to budgets.
quote: Using the results of control account variance analysis and indirect performance evaluations, update the control account estimates at completion to reflect future resource requirements to complete the remaining authorized work and, by comparing to budgets, calculate the variance at completion.

statement: The estimate at completion is the actual cost of work performed to date plus the estimate to complete for the remaining authorized work.
quote: The EAC is based on the Actual Cost of Work Performed (ACWP) to date plus the ETC for the remaining authorized work.

statement: Control account and summary level planning package estimates at completion are not constrained by funding, negotiated contract costs, or factored budgets.
quote: EACs are not constrained by funding, negotiated contract costs, or factored budgets (see Guideline 25).

statement: The variance at completion is the difference between the budget at completion and the estimate at completion for a control account or summary level planning package.
quote: Differences between the Budget at Completion (BAC) and EAC result in the CA and SLPP Variance at Completion (VAC).

statement: The variance at completion is calculated at least at the control account and summary level planning package levels.
quote: At a minimum, the VAC is calculated at the control account and SLPP levels.

statement: The guideline's purpose is to ensure that program performance status can be accurately summarized from the control account, at a minimum, through the work breakdown structure and organizational breakdown structure, for management insight and control and to meet customer reporting requirements.
quote: To ensure that program performance status can be accurately summarized from the control account (at a minimum) through the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and Organizational Breakdown Structure (OBS) for program management insight and control as well as to meet customer reporting requirements.

statement: The data that is summarized through the work breakdown structure and organizational breakdown structure from the control account through the contract level is comprised of budgeted cost for work scheduled, budgeted cost for work performed, actual cost of work performed, budget at completion, and estimate at completion.
quote: comprised of Budgeted Cost for Work Scheduled (BCWS), Budgeted Cost for Work Performed (BCWP), Actual Cost of Work Performed (ACWP), Budget at Completion (BAC), and Estimate at Completion (EAC) that is summarized through the WBS and OBS from the control account through the contract level.

statement: The data used for internal management control and for external customer reporting must be derived from the same data resident in the earned value management system.
quote: It is critical that data used for internal management control and external customer reporting are derived from the same data resident in the EVMS.

statement: The guideline's purpose is to ensure that all levels of program management review performance measurement data, implement corrective action management plans, and use the information for decision making.
quote: To ensure all levels of program management are reviewing performance measurement data, implementing corrective action management plans, and using the information for decision-making purposes.

statement: A corrective action management plan indicates that the program manager has recognized a cost or schedule variance significant enough to require management actions through a closed-loop corrective action process that runs from identification through closure.
quote: Corrective action management plans indicate the program manager has recognized a cost or schedule variance is significant enough to require management actions through a closed-loop (identification through closure) corrective action management process.

statement: Corrective action management plans state what, how, who, and when for the management actions taken to address identified root causes, and the plans are documented, implemented, and monitored until the problem is resolved.
quote: Corrective action management plans provide what, how, who, and when relative to management action(s) that are taken to address identified root causes and minimize their impact(s). The plans are documented, implemented, and monitored until resolution of the problem.

statement: The program's internal reports and the reports forwarded to the customer must indicate the overall cost and schedule impacts of program issues.
quote: The program’s internal reports and reports forwarded to the customer must indicate the overall cost and schedule impacts of program issues.

statement: The program manager's estimate at completion includes a range of estimates, and the most likely estimate is considered the official management estimate at completion.
quote: The program manager's EAC includes a range of estimates: Best Case, Worst Case, and Most Likely, from which the Most Likely EAC is considered the official Management EAC.

statement: At least monthly, the program manager's assessment of the contract-level forecast builds upon the performance measurement baseline level estimate at completion, updated monthly, or the comprehensive estimate at completion, and results in the management estimate at completion.
quote: At least monthly, the program manager's assessment of contract-level forecast builds upon the Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) level EAC updated monthly or from the Comprehensive EAC (CEAC) and results in the Management EAC.

statement: The management estimate at completion accounts for dollarized risks and opportunities that are tracked at the program level but have not yet been realized or incorporated into control accounts.
quote: The Management EAC accounts for dollarized risks and opportunities that are related to the risk management process and are tracked at the program level but have not yet been realized or incorporated into control accounts.

statement: At least annually, or more frequently if performance indicates the current estimate is invalid, a comprehensive or bottom-up estimate at completion is assessed at the contract level.
quote: At least annually, or more frequently if performance indicates that the current estimate is invalid, an assessment of the contract level EAC, also known as a comprehensive or bottom-up EAC, is accomplished.

statement: The externally reported estimate at completion and the internal estimate at completion reconcile and have a clear, consistent relationship.
quote: Contractor’s externally reported EAC and internal EAC reconcile and have a clear consistent relationship based on the identified risks/opportunities or other identified factors.

statement: When incorporating a customer directed change prior to negotiation, the work is planned based on the estimated value of the scope.
quote: When incorporating a customer directed change prior to negotiation, plan the work based on the estimated value of the scope.

statement: Undistributed budget is distributed to summary level planning packages and control accounts in a timely manner following authorization to proceed for a change order, letter contract, or negotiations and definitization of a contract action.
quote: Undistributed Budget (UB) is distributed to Summary Level Planning Packages (SLPPs) and control accounts in a timely manner following Authorization to Proceed (ATP) for a change order, letter contract, or negotiations and definitization of a contract action.

statement: Changes should never result in negative undistributed budget or management reserve values.
quote: Changes should never result in negative UB or MR values (see Guideline 12).

statement: Authorized changes are incorporated into the performance measurement baseline, and authorization documents are updated accordingly, before the commencement of work.
quote: Authorized changes are incorporated into the PMB and authorization documents updated accordingly before the commencement of work.

statement: Internal replanning is intended to maintain an executable baseline for the remaining in-scope work on the contract.
quote: Internal replanning is intended to maintain an executable baseline for the remaining in-scope work on the contract.

statement: Contract budget logs provide traceability of authorized baseline changes.
quote: Contract budget log(s) provide traceability of authorized baseline changes.

statement: The system description must describe and establish a freeze period suitable for forward planning discipline and the integrity of the performance measurement baseline.
quote: the system description must describe and establish a freeze period suitable for forward planning discipline and the integrity of the PMB.

statement: Baseline changes within the freeze period are limited, for example to customer-directed contract actions, rate changes, and economic price adjustments.
quote: Baseline changes within the freeze period are limited (e.g., customer-directed contract actions, rate changes, and economic price adjustments)

statement: The contractor should define the process for internal replanning related to setting budgeted cost for work scheduled equal to budgeted cost for work performed, not the reverse, when eliminating schedule variances for in-process work.
quote: The contractor should define the process for internal replanning, related to setting Budgeted Cost for Work Scheduled (BCWS) equal to Budgeted Cost for Work Performed (BCWP) (not the reverse) when eliminating schedule variances for in-process work.

statement: Retroactive adjustments are made only for correction of errors, routine accounting adjustments, or the effects of customer or management directed changes, including implementation of a single point adjustment.
quote: Adjustments are made only for correction of errors, routine accounting adjustments, or effects of customer or management directed changes, including implementation of a single point adjustment.

statement: Retroactive changes involve adjustments to previously reported values for budgeted cost for work scheduled, budgeted cost for work performed, or actual cost of work performed, related to completed work.
quote: Retroactive changes involve adjustments to previously reported values for Budgeted Cost for Work Scheduled (BCWS), Budgeted Cost for Work Performed (BCWP), or Actual Cost of Work Performed (ACWP) related to completed work (see Guideline 25).

statement: A single point adjustment is implemented sparingly and sets some or all existing contract cost or schedule variances to zero, typically accompanying a replan of all remaining effort that results in a new performance measurement baseline.
quote: A single point adjustment is implemented sparingly and is the process that sets some or all existing contract cost or schedule variances to zero and typically accompanies a replan of all remaining effort resulting in a new PMB.

statement: The contractor provides advance notification to the contracting officer before implementation of a single point adjustment.
quote: The contractor provides advance notification to the contracting officer before implementation of an SPA.

statement: When necessary, a total program budget greater than the contract budget base, called an over-target baseline, or a total program schedule exceeding the contractual period of performance, called an over-target schedule, is proposed, documented, and established to support management of the remaining authorized work.
quote: When necessary, propose, document, and establish a total program budget greater than the contract budget base (over-target baseline) and/or a total program schedule exceeding the contractual period of performance (over-target schedule) to support management of the remaining authorized work.

statement: Advance notification must be provided to the customer before an over-target baseline or over-target schedule is implemented.
quote: (over-target baseline) and/or a total program schedule exceeding the contractual period of performance (over-target schedule) to support management of the remaining authorized work. Advance notification must be provided to the customer prior to implementation.

statement: The contract budget base is a controlled value and cannot be changed by the contractor except as a result of customer contract actions.
quote: The CBB is a controlled value and cannot be changed by the contractor except as a result of customer contract actions.

statement: Requests for establishing an over-target baseline or an over-target schedule are initiated by the contractor and approved by the customer contracting authority.
quote: Requests for establishing an OTB or an OTS are initiated by the contractor and approved by the customer contracting authority.

statement: Implementing an over-target baseline or over-target schedule does not change the terms and conditions of the contract but merely serves to improve management of the remaining work.
quote: Implementing an OTB or OTS does not change the terms and conditions of the contract but merely serves to improve management of the remaining work.

statement: The work breakdown structure includes all program elements, such as hardware, software, services, data or facilities, and is decomposed to lower levels for planning, budgeting, scheduling, cost accounting, work authorization, measuring progress and management control purposes.
quote: The WBS includes all program elements (e.g., hardware, software, services, data, or facilities) and is decomposed to lower levels for planning, budgeting, scheduling, cost accounting, work authorization, measuring progress, and management control purposes

statement: Using a product-oriented work breakdown structure facilitates data collection and traceability and provides a control framework for integrated program management, work authorization, tracking and reporting purposes.
quote: It facilitates data collection and traceability and provides a control framework for integrated program management, work authorization, tracking, and reporting purposes.

statement: The unique coding allows data derived from one management system to relate to and be consistent with the data of each of the other systems, at the level established by the unique coding or charge number level through the total contract level.
quote: This will allow the data derived from one system to relate to and be consistent with the data of each of the other systems at the level established by the unique coding and/or charge number level through the total contract level

statement: Objective performance data tied to technical milestones provides management with accurate progress visibility and early indicators of program risks requiring corrective action.
quote: Objective performance data, tied to technical milestones, provides management with accurate progress visibility and early indicators of program risks requiring corrective action.

statement: The logical sequence of the schedule is horizontally and vertically integrated.
quote: The logical sequence of the schedule is horizontally and vertically integrated.

statement: The Integrated Master Schedule contains all authorized discrete work assigned to the program organizational elements, including subcontractors, that are responsible for performing the work consistent with the work breakdown structure.
quote: It contains all authorized discrete work assigned to program organizational elements, including subcontractors, responsible for performing the work consistent with the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS).

statement: Schedule margin, if used, may not represent any specific scope or resources and may not be used to assess earned value performance.
quote: may not represent any specific scope or resources, and may not be used to assess earned value performance.

statement: Formally authorizing work ensures that the assignment of program work scope to the responsible organization is documented, and that the resources required to complete the work are budgeted and acknowledged by the management team before the work starts.

statement: For collateral savings, the Contracting Officer determines a rate from 20 to 100 percent that applies to any projected collateral savings determined to be realized in a typical year of use, after subtracting any Government costs not previously offset.
quote: by a rate from 20 to 100 percent, as determined by the Contracting Officer, of any projected collateral savings determined to be realized in a typical year of use after subtracting any Government costs not previously offset.

statement: The Contractor's share of collateral savings will not exceed the contract's firm-fixed-price, target price, target cost, or estimated cost at the time the VECP is accepted, or $100,000, whichever is greater.
quote: However, the Contractor's share of collateral savings will not exceed the contract's firm-fixed-price, target price, target cost, or estimated cost, at the time the VECP is accepted, or $100,000, whichever is greater.

statement: The Contractor shall include an appropriate value engineering clause in any subcontract valued at or above the simplified acquisition threshold, as defined in FAR 2.101 on the date of subcontract award, and may include one in subcontracts of lesser value.
quote: The Contractor shall include an appropriate value engineering clause in any subcontract-valued at or above the simplified acquisition threshold, as defined in FAR 2.101 on the date of subcontract award, and may include one in subcontracts of lesser value.

statement: If additional time is required, the Contracting Officer will notify the Contractor within the 45-day period and provide the reason for the delay and the expected date of the decision.
quote: If additional time is required, the Contracting Officer will notify the Contractor within the 45-day period and provide the reason for the delay and the expected date of the decision.

statement: Changes in the place of performance of any make items in the program are subject to the requirement to notify the Contracting Officer in writing and submit justification in sufficient detail to permit evaluation.
quote: (1) notify the Contracting Officer in writing, and (2) submit justification in sufficient detail to permit evaluation. Changes in the place of performance of any “make” items in the program are subject to this requirement.

statement: Modification of the make-or-buy program to incorporate proposed changes or additions shall be effective upon the Contractor's receipt of the Contracting Officer's written approval.
quote: (c) Modification of the make-or-buy program to incorporate proposed changes or additions shall be effective upon the Contractor's receipt of the Contracting Officer's written approval.

statement: Under Alternate I, a Contractor that desires to reverse the make or buy categorization of an item designated in the contract as subject to the paragraph shall support its proposal with certified cost or pricing data when required by FAR 15.403 and with data other than certified cost or pricing data to permit evaluation.
quote: designated in the contract as subject to this paragraph, it shall— (1) Support its proposal with certified cost or pricing data in accordance with FAR 15.408, Table 15-2 when required by FAR 15.403, and data other than certified cost or pricing data, to permit evaluation; and

statement: Alternate II adds a paragraph (d) to the basic clause under which a Contractor that desires to reverse the make or buy categorization of an item designated in the contract as subject to that paragraph shall do the listed things.
quote: Alternate II (OCT 2010). As prescribed in 15.408(a)(2), add the following paragraph (d) to the basic clause: (d) If the Contractor desires to reverse the categorization of “make” or “buy” for any item or items designated in the contract as subject to this paragraph, it shall—

statement: One listed duty under Alternate II is, after approval is granted, to promptly negotiate with the Contracting Officer an equitable reduction in the contract's total estimated cost and fee in accordance with the named paragraph of the Incentive Fee clause.
quote: (2) After approval is granted, promptly negotiate with the Contracting Officer an equitable reduction in the contract's total estimated cost and fee in accordance with paragraph (e) of the Incentive Fee clause of this contract.

statement: The offeror's proposal shall exclude excessive pass-through charges.
quote: (b) General. The offeror's proposal shall exclude excessive pass-through charges.

statement: Under the Allowable Cost and Payment clause, a contractor must submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal within 6 months after the end of each fiscal year; the clause allows reasonable extensions for exceptional circumstances only.
quote: within the 6-month period following the expiration of each of its fiscal years
note: RFO 52.216-7 (S-0020) has the same wording; DoD uses it under Class Deviation 2026-O0038.

statement: Contracting officer determination applies to business units of a multidivisional corporation under the cognizance of a corporate administrative contracting officer, who is responsible for the determination and is assisted, as required, by the administrative contracting officers assigned to the individual business units.
quote: Business units of a multidivisional corporation under the cognizance of a corporate administrative contracting officer (see subpart 42.6), with that officer responsible for the determination, assisted, as required, by the administrative contracting officers assigned to the individual business units.

statement: For business units not under a corporate administrative contracting officer but having a resident one, a nonresident administrative contracting officer is considered resident for this purpose if at least 75 percent of that officer's time is devoted to a single contractor.
quote: a nonresident administrative contracting officer is considered as resident if at least 75 percent of the administrative contracting officer's time is devoted to a single contractor

statement: Under the Allowable Cost and Payment clause, the contractor must submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal to the contracting officer or cognizant Federal agency official and to the cognizant auditor.
quote: the contractor is required to submit an adequate final indirect cost rate proposal to the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and to the cognizant auditor.

statement: Each contractor must submit its final indirect cost rate proposal within 6 months following the expiration of each of its fiscal years.
quote: Each contractor is required to submit the final indirect cost rate proposal within the six-month period following the expiration of each of its fiscal years.

statement: The contracting officer may grant reasonable extensions in writing only for exceptional circumstances and only when the contractor requests them in writing.
quote: The contracting officer may grant, in writing, reasonable extensions, for exceptional circumstances only, when requested in writing by the contractor.

statement: The cognizant auditor reviews the adequacy of the contractor's proposal for audit and gives the contractor and contracting officer a written description of any inadequacies.
quote: The cognizant auditor will review the adequacy of the contractor's proposal for audit in support of negotiating final indirect cost rates and will provide a written description of any inadequacies to the contractor and contracting officer.

statement: The contracting officer or cognizant Federal agency official heads the Government negotiating team, which includes the cognizant auditor and technical or functional personnel as required.
quote: The contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) shall head the Government negotiating team, which includes the cognizant auditor and technical or functional personnel as required.

statement: The negotiation memorandum must reconcile all costs questioned, identifying the items and amounts allowed or disallowed in the final settlement.
quote: reconciliation of all costs questioned, with identification of items and amounts allowed or disallowed in the final settlement

statement: The contracting officer must notify the contractor of the individual costs considered unallowable and the respective amounts of the disallowance.
quote: Notify the contractor of the individual costs which were considered unallowable and the respective amounts of the disallowance.

statement: The cognizant contracting officer prepares a written indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts.
quote: Prepare a written indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts

statement: When the listed conditions are met, the contracting officer responsible for closeout negotiates the settlement of the direct and indirect costs of a specific contract, task order or delivery order in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates.
quote: shall negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed, in advance of the determination of final direct costs

statement: The contract, task order or delivery order must be physically complete before the quick-closeout procedure may be used.
quote: (1) The contract, task order, or delivery order is physically complete

statement: Unsettled direct and indirect costs are considered relatively insignificant when the total to be allocated to any one contract, task order or delivery order does not exceed the lesser of $1,000,000 or 10 percent, measured as stated in the next claim.
quote: Cost amounts will be considered relatively insignificant when the total unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order does not exceed the lesser of— (i) $1,000,000; or (ii) 10 percent

statement: The 10 percent limit is measured against the total contract, task order or delivery order amount.
quote: (ii) 10 percent of the total contract, task order, or delivery order amount

statement: The risk assessment must include consideration of the contractor's accounting, estimating and purchasing systems and of other concerns of the cognizant contract auditors.
quote: The risk assessment shall include— (i) Consideration of the contractor's accounting, estimating, and purchasing systems; (ii) Other concerns of the cognizant contract auditors

statement: The risk assessment may also weigh other pertinent information, such as the documented history of approved indirect cost rate agreements, changes to the contractor's rate structure, volatility of rate fluctuations, and mergers or acquisitions.
quote: Any other pertinent information, such as, documented history of Federal Government approved indirect cost rate agreements, changes to contractor's rate structure, volatility of rate fluctuations during affected periods, mergers or acquisitions

statement: Agreement must also be reached on a reasonable estimate of allocable dollars.
quote: Agreement can be reached on a reasonable estimate of allocable dollars

statement: A quick-closeout determination of final indirect costs is final for the contract it covers, and no adjustment is made to other contracts for over- or under-recoveries of costs allocated to that contract.
quote: shall be final for the contract it covers and no adjustment shall be made to other contracts for over- or under-recoveries of costs allocated or allocable to the contract covered by the agreement

statement: Indirect cost rates used in a quick closeout are not a binding precedent when final indirect cost rates are established for other contracts.
quote: Indirect cost rates used in the quick closeout of a contract shall not be considered a binding precedent when establishing the final indirect cost rates for other contracts

statement: Negotiation of a forward pricing rate agreement may be requested by the contracting officer or the contractor, or initiated by the administrative contracting officer.
quote: Negotiation of forward pricing rate agreements (FPRA's) may be requested by the contracting officer or the contractor or initiated by the administrative contracting officer (ACO)

statement: The cognizant contract administration agency determines whether a forward pricing rate agreement will be established.
quote: The cognizant contract administration agency shall determine whether an FPRA will be established

statement: In deciding whether to establish an agreement, the administrative contracting officer should consider whether the benefits are commensurate with the effort of establishing and monitoring it.
quote: In determining whether or not to establish such an agreement, the ACO should consider whether the benefits to be derived from the agreement are commensurate with the effort of establishing and monitoring it

statement: Agreements are normally negotiated only with contractors having a significant volume of Government contract proposals.
quote: Normally, FPRA's should be negotiated only with contractors having a significant volume of Government contract proposals

statement: The administrative contracting officer requires the contractor's forward pricing rate proposal to include cost or pricing data that are accurate, complete and current as of the date of submission, subject to the cross-reference to 15.407-3(c).
quote: require that it include cost or pricing data that are accurate, complete, and current as of the date of submission (but see 15.407-3(c)).

statement: After negotiations the administrative contracting officer prepares a price negotiation memorandum and forwards copies of it and of the agreement to the cognizant auditor and to contracting offices known to be affected.
quote: the ACO shall prepare a price negotiation memorandum (PNM) (see 15.406-3) and forward copies of the PNM and FPRA to the cognizant auditor and to all contracting offices that are known to be affected by the FPRA.

statement: The agreement provides for cancellation at the option of either party and requires the contractor to report any significant change in the cost or pricing data supporting it to the administrative contracting officer and the cognizant auditor.
quote: The agreement shall provide for cancellation at the option of either party and shall require the contractor to submit to the ACO and to the cognizant contract auditor any significant change in cost or pricing data used to support the FPRA.

statement: If no agreement has been established, or an established one has been invalidated, the administrative contracting officer issues a forward pricing rate recommendation to buying activities with documentation to assist negotiators.
quote: If an FPRA has not been established or has been invalidated, the ACO will issue a forward pricing rate recommendation (FPRR) to buying activities with documentation to assist negotiators

statement: When an agreement is invalid, the contractor should submit and negotiate a new proposal to reflect the changed conditions.
quote: When an FPRA is invalid, the contractor should submit and negotiate a new proposal to reflect the changed conditions

statement: A cost may not be charged as a direct cost to a final cost objective if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included in an indirect cost pool allocated to that or any other final cost objective.
quote: No final cost objective shall have allocated to it as a direct cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included in any indirect cost pool

statement: Direct costs of the contract must be charged directly to the contract.
quote: Direct costs of the contract shall be charged directly to the contract.

statement: Costs specifically identified with other final cost objectives of the contractor are direct costs of those cost objectives, and are not charged to the contract directly or indirectly.
quote: All costs specifically identified with other final cost objectives of the contractor are direct costs of those cost objectives and are not to be charged to the contract directly or indirectly.

statement: For reasons of practicality, the contractor may treat any direct cost of a minor dollar amount as an indirect cost if the accounting treatment is consistently applied to all final cost objectives and produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.
quote: (b) For reasons of practicality, the contractor may treat any direct cost of a minor dollar amount as an indirect cost if the accounting treatment— (1) Is consistently applied to all final cost objectives; and (2) Produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.

statement: Treating a minor direct cost as an indirect cost is allowed only when the treatment is consistently applied to all final cost objectives and produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.
quote: (1) Is consistently applied to all final cost objectives; and (2) Produces substantially the same results as treating the cost as a direct cost.

statement: For contracts subject to full CAS coverage, allocation of indirect costs is based on the applicable CAS provisions; for all other contracts, the CAS provisions in paragraphs (b) through (h) of the section apply.
quote: For contracts subject to full CAS coverage, allocation of indirect costs shall be based on the applicable provisions. For all other contracts, the applicable CAS provisions in paragraphs (b) through (h) of this section apply.

statement: Indirect costs are the costs remaining to be allocated to intermediate or two or more final cost objectives, after direct costs have been determined and charged directly to the contract or other work.
quote: After direct costs have been determined and charged directly to the contract or other work, indirect costs are those remaining to be allocated to intermediate or two or more final cost objectives.

statement: A cost may not be charged as an indirect cost to a final cost objective if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances have been included as a direct cost of that or any other final cost objective.
quote: No final cost objective shall have allocated to it as an indirect cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, have been included as a direct cost

statement: The contractor accumulates indirect costs by logical cost groupings, giving due consideration to the reasons for incurring the costs.
quote: The contractor shall accumulate indirect costs by logical cost groupings with due consideration of the reasons for incurring such costs.

statement: Each cost grouping is determined to permit an allocation base that is common to all cost objectives to which the grouping is allocated.
quote: The contractor shall determine each grouping so as to permit use of an allocation base that is common to all cost objectives to which the grouping is to be allocated.

statement: Once an accepted base for allocating indirect costs exists, the contractor must not fragment the base by removing individual elements.
quote: Once an appropriate base for allocating indirect costs has been accepted, the contractor shall not fragment the base by removing individual elements.

statement: All items properly includable in an indirect cost base bear a pro rata share of indirect costs, whether or not they are accepted as Government contract costs.
quote: All items properly includable in an indirect cost base shall bear a pro rata share of indirect costs irrespective of their acceptance as Government contract costs.

statement: For contracts other than those subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the base period for allocating indirect costs is the contractor's fiscal year used for financial reporting purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.
quote: (2) For contracts other than those subject to paragraph (g)(1) of this section, the base period for allocating indirect costs shall be the contractor's fiscal year used for financial reporting purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.

statement: The cognizant Government auditor establishes final indirect cost rates for business units not covered in 42.705-1(a).
quote: The cognizant Government auditor shall establish final indirect cost rates for business units not covered in 42.705-1(a).

statement: Once a proposal has been determined adequate for audit in support of negotiating final indirect cost rates, the auditor audits the proposal and prepares an advisory audit report, including a listing of any relevant advance agreements or restrictive terms of specific contracts.
quote: (2) Once a proposal has been determined to be adequate for audit in support of negotiating final indirect cost rates, the auditor shall— (i) Audit the proposal and prepare an advisory audit report, including a listing of any relevant advance agreements or restrictive terms of specific contracts;

statement: The auditor seeks agreement on indirect costs with the contractor and prepares an indirect cost rate agreement that the contractor and the auditor both sign.
quote: Seek agreement on indirect costs with the contractor; (iii) Prepare an indirect cost rate agreement conforming to the requirements of the contracts. The agreement shall be signed by the contractor and the auditor

statement: If agreement with the contractor is not reached, the auditor forwards the audit report to the contracting officer, who resolves the disagreement.
quote: If agreement with the contractor is not reached, forward the audit report to the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) identified in the Directory of Contract Administration Services Components (see 42.203), who will then resolve the disagreement

statement: A proposal is not accepted and no agreement to establish final indirect cost rates is made unless the contractor has certified the costs.
quote: a proposal shall not be accepted and no agreement shall be made to establish final indirect cost rates unless the costs have been certified by the contractor.

statement: The agency head or designee may waive the certification requirement when it is determined to be in the interest of the United States and the reasons for the determination are put in writing and made available to the public.
quote: (1) The agency head, or designee, may waive the certification requirement when— (i) It is determined to be in the interest of the United States; and (ii) The reasons for the determination are put in writing and made available to the public.

statement: If the contractor has not certified its proposal for final indirect cost rates and a waiver is not appropriate, the contracting officer may unilaterally establish the rates.
quote: If the contractor has not certified its proposal for final indirect cost rates and a waiver is not appropriate, the contracting officer may unilaterally establish the rates.

statement: Rates established unilaterally should be based on audited historical data or other available data as long as unallowable costs are excluded, and set low enough to ensure that unallowable costs will not be reimbursed.
quote: (i) Based on audited historical data or other available data as long as unallowable costs are excluded; and (ii) Set low enough to ensure that unallowable costs will not be reimbursed.

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(2) of the section, the clause at 52.242-4, Certification of Final Indirect Costs, is incorporated into all solicitations and contracts that provide for establishment of final indirect cost rates.
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(2) of this subsection, the clause at 52.242-4, Certification of Final Indirect Costs, shall be incorporated into all solicitations and contracts which provide for establishment of final indirect cost rates.

statement: For contracts subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the contractor follows the criteria and guidance in 48 CFR 9904.406 for selecting the cost accounting periods used in allocating indirect costs.
quote: (1) For contracts subject to full or modified CAS coverage, the contractor shall follow the criteria and guidance in 48 CFR 9904.406 for selecting the cost accounting periods to be used in allocating indirect costs.

statement: The fiscal year used as the base period will normally be 12 months, but a different period may be appropriate, for example when a change in fiscal year occurs due to a business combination or other circumstances.
quote: The fiscal year will normally be 12 months, but a different period may be appropriate (e.g., when a change in fiscal year occurs due to a business combination or other circumstances).

statement: Auditor determination may also be used for business units covered in 42.705-1(a) when the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and the auditor agree that the indirect costs can be settled with little difficulty and any of the listed circumstances applies.
quote: (2) In addition, auditor determination may be used for business units that are covered in 42.705-1(a) when the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and auditor agree that the indirect costs can be settled with little difficulty and any of the following circumstances apply:

statement: One circumstance for auditor determination of a business unit covered in 42.705-1(a) is that the unit has primarily fixed-price contracts with only minor involvement in cost-reimbursement contracts; another is that the administrative cost of contracting officer determination would exceed the expected benefits.
quote: (i) The business unit has primarily fixed-price contracts, with only minor involvement in cost-reimbursement contracts. (ii) The administrative cost of contracting officer determination would exceed the expected benefits.

statement: Two further circumstances for auditor determination of a business unit covered in 42.705-1(a) are that the unit has no history of disputes and few cost problems, or that the contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and the auditor agree that special circumstances require auditor determination.
quote: (iii) The business unit does not have a history of disputes and there are few cost problems. (iv) The contracting officer (or cognizant Federal agency official) and auditor agree that special circumstances require auditor determination.

statement: A waiver of the certification requirement may be appropriate for a contract with a foreign government or international organization, or with a State or local government subject to the OMB Uniform Guidance.
quote: (2) A waiver may be appropriate for a contract with— (i) A foreign government or international organization, such as a subsidiary body of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization; (ii) A State or local government subject to the OMB Uniform Guidance at 2 CFR part 200, subpart E and appendices V and VII

statement: The Department of Energy may provide an alternate clause in its agency supplement for its Management and Operating contracts.
quote: (2) The Department of Energy may provide an alternate clause in its agency supplement for its Management and Operating contracts.

statement: A billing rate is an indirect cost rate established temporarily for interim reimbursement of incurred indirect costs and adjusted as necessary until final indirect cost rates are established.
quote: Billing rate as used in this subpart means an indirect cost rate (1) established temporarily for interim reimbursement of incurred indirect costs and (2) adjusted as necessary pending establishment of final indirect cost rates.

statement: Establishing final indirect cost rates gives a uniform approach with a contractor when more than one contract or agency is involved, economy of administration, and timely settlement under cost-reimbursement contracts.
quote: Establishing final indirect cost rates under this subpart provides— (1) Uniformity of approach with a contractor when more than one contract or agency is involved; (2) Economy of administration; and (3) Timely settlement under cost-reimbursement contracts.

statement: A single agency is responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit, and those rates bind all agencies and their contracting offices unless a statute specifically prohibits that.
quote: A single agency (see 42.705-1) shall be responsible for establishing final indirect cost rates for each business unit. These rates shall be binding on all agencies and their contracting offices, unless otherwise specifically prohibited by statute.

statement: An agency does not perform its own audit of indirect cost rates when the contracting officer determines that the audit objectives can reasonably be met by accepting the results of an audit conducted by another department or agency of the Federal Government.
quote: An agency shall not perform an audit of indirect cost rates when the contracting officer determines that the objectives of the audit can reasonably be met by accepting the results of an audit that was conducted by any other department or agency of the Federal Government

statement: Billing rates and final indirect cost rates are used to reimburse indirect costs under cost-reimbursement contracts and to determine progress payments under fixed-price contracts.
quote: (b) Billing rates and final indirect cost rates shall be used in reimbursing indirect costs under cost-reimbursement contracts and in determining progress payments under fixed-price contracts.

statement: Final indirect cost rates are used for contract closeout for a business unit unless the quick-closeout procedure is used.
quote: Final indirect cost rates shall be used for contract closeout for a business unit, unless the quick-closeout procedure in 42.708 is used.

statement: Those final rates bind all cost-reimbursement contracts at the business unit, subject to any specific limitation in a contract or advance agreement.
quote: These final rates shall be binding for all cost-reimbursement contracts at the business unit, subject to any specific limitation in a contract or advance agreement

statement: Final indirect cost rates are used in negotiating the final price of fixed-price incentive and fixed-price redeterminable contracts, and in other situations requiring indirect costs to be settled before contract prices are established, unless the quick-closeout procedure is used.
quote: shall be used in negotiating the final price of fixed-price incentive and fixed-price redeterminable contracts and in other situations requiring that indirect costs be settled before contract prices are established, unless the quick-closeout procedure in 42.708 is used.

statement: When cost sharing is authorized, the arrangement may require the contractor to participate in the costs of the contract by accepting indirect cost rates lower than the anticipated actual rates.
quote: (a) Cost-sharing arrangements, when authorized, may call for the contractor to participate in the costs of the contract by accepting indirect cost rates lower than the anticipated actual rates.

statement: In a cost-sharing arrangement a negotiated indirect cost rate ceiling may be incorporated into the contract for prospective application.
quote: In such cases, a negotiated indirect cost rate ceiling may be incorporated into the contract for prospective application.

statement: One example of a situation where a final indirect cost rate ceiling may be prudent is a new or recently reorganized company with no past or recent record of incurred indirect costs.
quote: Other situations may make it prudent to provide a final indirect cost rate ceiling in a contract. Examples of such circumstances are when the proposed contractor— (i) Is a new or recently reorganized company, and there is no past or recent record of incurred indirect costs;

statement: In such cases an equitable ceiling covering the final indirect cost rates may be negotiated and specified in the contract.
quote: In such cases, an equitable ceiling covering the final indirect cost rates may be negotiated and specified in the contract.

statement: When ceiling provisions are used, the contract must also provide that the Government will not be obligated to pay any additional amount if the final indirect cost rates exceed the negotiated ceiling rates.
quote: When ceiling provisions are utilized, the contract shall also provide that (1) the Government will not be obligated to pay any additional amount should the final indirect cost rates exceed the negotiated ceiling rates

statement: When the final indirect cost rates are less than the negotiated ceiling rates, the negotiated rates are reduced to conform with the lower rates.
quote: (2) in the event the final indirect cost rates are less than the negotiated ceiling rates, the negotiated rates will be reduced to conform with the lower rates.

statement: Defense Contract Management Agency administrative contracting officers are authorized to negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates.
quote: Defense Contract Management Agency administrative contracting officers are authorized to negotiate the settlement of direct and indirect costs for a specific contract, task order, or delivery order to be closed in advance of the determination of final direct costs and indirect rates

statement: That authority applies regardless of the dollar value or percentage of unsettled direct or indirect costs allocable to the contract, task order, or delivery order.
quote: regardless of the dollar value or percentage of unsettled direct or indirect costs allocable to the contract, task order, or delivery order.

statement: In lieu of the thresholds in the FAR quick-closeout procedure, the DoD supplement treats unsettled direct and indirect costs as relatively insignificant under its own test.
quote: (2) In lieu of the thresholds at FAR 42.708(a)(2)(i) and (ii), the amount of unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to the contract, task order, or delivery order will be considered relatively insignificant

statement: Under that test the unsettled costs are relatively insignificant when the total allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order does not exceed $2 million, regardless of the total contract amount.
quote: when the total unsettled direct costs and indirect costs to be allocated to any one contract, task order, or delivery order do not exceed $2 million, regardless of the total contract, task order, or delivery order amount.
